tb_random_dropout — 2D typed op

• Data kinds: points → points

• Call: fullseye.apply(img, "tb_random_dropout", a=0.5, b=0.5) (the 2-D model is one image plus two scalar knobs a,b∈[0,1])

Usage

Randomly removes a ratio fraction of the points and returns (kept, kept_idx) (mimicking missing data).

The number of points kept is round((1-ratio)*N). kept_idx are ascending indices into the original array, and kept == points[kept_idx] holds exactly. Reproduces in training the point loss caused by occlusion / sparse viewpoints. Requires 0 <= ratio <= 1.

ratio outside [0,1] raises ValueError. ratio=1 gives an empty (0,3) and an empty index array, ratio=0 gives all points (in their original order). The number of points kept is decided by Python's round (round half to even), so at the .5 boundary it leans to the even side. seed fixes the permutation, so it is deterministic. Returns (kept float64 (M,3), kept_idx int64 (M,)). The removal is spatially uniform; to imitate local loss (occlusion) use cutout.

The 3d op random_dropout bridged into the 2-D evolution registry. The implementation is the same; only the calling convention is adapted to op(v, a, b). This op has no tunable parameters; neither a nor b is used.
